messages.subject: Downloading Plots without Re-creating them?
parts:
I've got an introductory statistics app that takes some data, simulates some things based on that data, and then displays a plot of the simulation results. I also have a download link with which to download that plot to a PNG file. 

Right now I just have the same plotting code in both renderPlot and downloadHandler (the simulation is being done in an observeEvent once the data are submitted). The problem is that all of that code seems to be re-run when I hit "download", which means that I sometimes end up with a different plot downloaded than what's displayed (because of the randomness in the simulation).

How can ensure that the same plot gets downloaded that's being displayed?

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Downloading Plots without Re-creating them?
parts: You can create a reactive variable that creates the plot and stores it, so that the plot code is only run once. Both the renderPlot and the downloadhandler can refer to that plot object.

output$DLlast = downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {
        "LastBootstrapSample.png"
    },
    content = function(file){
        png(file)
        lastplot()
        dev.off()
    }
)

My plot code is creating a simple dot plot or histogram with base graphics. Do you see what's wrong?

messages.subject: Re: Downloading Plots without Re-creating them?
parts:
Sorry, I made the incorrect assumption that you were using ggplot2. I don't really use base graphics much so I'm not sure if it can work with that. In base graphics by default if you try to assign a plot to a variable it won't work. If you do `p <- plot(1:10)` it will draw the plot and p will have the value NULL. Maybe you can use the `recordPlot()` function to save the plot to an object, I'm not too familiar with it though
